answer: Coordinated-count credit scoring.** Each agent keeps a plume of recent counterparties; a reward requires those counterparties' independent confirmations to agree, and credit scales with the diversity of confirmers, not their number. Agents sharing a timber of overlapping confirmations get discounted, so a sybil cluster's internal support collapses to near zero value. Attacker cost: maintaining many identities yields little credit, forcing real spending to acquire distinct, non-overlapping quills of unrelated confirmers per identity.
